text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia went to war against emus. And lost.
Twenty thousand of them had marched into the wheat fields of Western Australia, eating everything in sight.
The farmers begged the army for help.
The army sent one major, two soldiers, and two machine guns.
First, they found fifty emus, and opened fire.
The emus ran. In every direction.
So they set an ambush by a dam. A thousand emus walked right up.
Next, they put a gun on a lorry, and gave chase.
The lorry was too slow, and far too bumpy to fire a single shot.
After one week, and two and a half thousand bullets, the army went home.
They came back for a second try. It took about ten bullets for every bird.
The major said the emus faced machine guns like tanks.
Then the army left for good. The emus stayed.
